8:["$","$L13",null,{"data":{"chapterId":13,"verseId":5,"chapterTitle":"Examination of Compounded Phenomena","totalVerses":8,"verseData":{"id":"v13_5","number":5,"title":"Neither Identity Nor Difference Changes","sanskrit":{"text":"","transliteration":"","translation":"A thing itself does not change. Something different does not change. Because a young man doesn't grow old, And because and an old man doesn't grow old either."},"philosophy":{"insight":"The identity/difference analysis applied to change: the SAME thing can't change (it would remain itself). A DIFFERENT thing can't change (it's already something else — no transformation occurred). A young man doesn't grow old (he's young, not old). An old man doesn't grow old (he's already old).","madhyamaka":"Identity horn: if the young man (as inherently young) becomes old, he retains his young-identity while being old — contradiction. Difference horn: if the old man is inherently different from the young man, no transformation occurred — one replaced the other. Neither inherent identity nor inherent difference accommodates change.","quantum":"Quantum jumps: electrons transition between discrete energy levels without passing through intermediate states. The electron doesn't \"gradually become\" the higher-energy state while remaining in the lower state. It jumps — the lower state ceases and the higher state begins. Change is discrete, not continuous transformation of identity.","bridge":"Both quantum jumps and Nāgārjuna's analysis show that change isn't smooth transformation of an enduring identity. States succeed each other — one ceases, another arises — without an inherent entity persisting through the change.","accessible":"A young man doesn't grow old while staying young (contradiction). An old man doesn't grow old because he's already old (no change needed). So who grows old? Neither the young nor the old — aging is a PROCESS of conventional succession, not transformation of an inherent identity.","twoTruths":"Conventionally, people age — the young man becomes old. Ultimately, no inherent \"young man\" transforms into an inherent \"old man.\" Conventional continuity is preserved; inherent transformation is denied.","commonMisconception":"NOT denying that aging happens. The young man conventionally becomes old. The point is that this change can't be explained through INHERENT identity or INHERENT difference. It works through conventional, dependent succession."},"quantumResonance":{"concept":"Quantum Jumps Between Discrete States","score":69,"strength":"Medium","explanation":"Electrons jump between energy levels without intermediate states — the lower state ceases, the higher begins. Like Nāgārjuna's analysis: the young state ceases, the old state arises. No inherent entity smoothly transforms. Change is succession, not transformation of identity.","caveat":"Quantum jumps are physical transitions with precise mathematical description. The parallel is about discrete succession of states rather than smooth identity transformation."},"animation":{"visualBridge":"An electron jumping between energy levels — the lower orbital disappears, the higher appears. No smooth transition, just discrete succession. Paralleled with a young face morphing to old through discrete stages.","educationalGoal":"User sees that change is succession of states, not smooth transformation of an enduring identity — whether in quantum systems or in aging."},"deeperDive":[{"q":"Why doesn't \"a thing itself\" change?","a":"If the \"young man\" is defined by his youth-identity, and that identity is inherent (fixed), then he can't become old while remaining \"himself.\" His inherent identity would prevent the transformation. The thing itself (defined by its inherent nature) can't become other than itself.","realLifeExample":"If you define yourself inherently as \"a student,\" then graduating makes you \"not yourself.\" Your inherent student-identity would resist change. But identities change because they're not inherent."},{"q":"Why doesn't \"something different\" change?","a":"If the old man is INHERENTLY different from the young man — a completely separate entity — then no transformation occurred. The young man just ceased, and a different entity (old man) appeared. That's replacement, not change. Change requires some continuity.","realLifeExample":"If you completely replace one employee with another, the first didn't \"become\" the second — they were replaced. Change requires connection, not complete disconnection."},{"q":"How do quantum jumps illustrate this?","a":"An electron in energy level E1 absorbs a photon and jumps to E2. It doesn't smoothly transition — E1 ceases and E2 begins. The electron doesn't remain \"in E1\" while becoming \"E2\" (identity), nor is the E2-electron a completely unrelated entity (difference). It's a quantum succession.","realLifeExample":"Switching TV channels: Channel 1 doesn't gradually become Channel 2. You're watching Channel 1, then suddenly Channel 2. The TV didn't \"transform\" — the state changed discretely."},{"q":"What is the youth/age example meant to show?","a":"It makes the abstract dilemma concrete and intuitive. Everyone understands aging. The young man (qua young) doesn't age — that contradicts his youth. The old man (qua old) doesn't age — he's already there. Yet aging happens conventionally. The puzzle dissolves when we drop the demand for inherent identity.","realLifeExample":"The caterpillar doesn't become a butterfly while remaining a caterpillar. The butterfly isn't a completely unrelated organism. Metamorphosis is a conventional process of dependent succession, not transformation of inherent identity."},{"q":"How does Mādhyamika explain aging without inherent identity?","a":"Aging is a conventional process: moment-by-moment, the aggregates change dependently. Each moment arises in dependence on the prior moment. There's conventional continuity (memory, physical resemblance, causal connection) without inherent identity persisting through time.","realLifeExample":"A river flows continuously — each moment's water is connected to (dependent on) the prior moment's water, but no single \"drop\" persists. The river \"ages\" through dependent succession, not through an inherent river-essence persisting."},{"q":"How does this connect to the Buddhist doctrine of momentariness?","a":"Buddhist momentariness (kṣaṇikavāda) holds that phenomena exist for a single moment, then cease. Change is the successive arising of momentary states. Nāgārjuna's analysis supports this: change isn't transformation of an enduring entity but succession of dependent moments.","deeper":"The identity/difference analysis here echoes Ch.2 (motion — the mover doesn't move, nor does the non-mover), Ch.10 (fire-fuel), and Ch.11 (birth-aging-death). The same logical structure is applied across domains: identity of agent/process fails, difference fails, and the resolution is conventional dependent succession. This universality demonstrates that the argument is about the STRUCTURE of inherent existence claims, not about specific topics."}],"quiz":{"beginner":{"question":"Why doesn't the young man grow old?","options":["A) People don't age","B) The young man (defined by youth) can't become old while remaining \"young\" — his youth-identity prevents it. And the old man is already old, so he doesn't grow old either.","C) Only old men grow old","D) Age is an illusion"],"correct":"B","explanation":"The identity horn: the young (qua young) can't become not-young. The difference horn: the old is already old. Neither inherent identity nor difference explains change. Change works conventionally through dependent succession."},"intermediate":{"question":"How do quantum jumps parallel the identity/difference analysis of change?","options":["A) No parallel","B) Electrons jump between states without smooth transition — the lower state ceases, the higher begins. No inherent identity persists through the \"change.\" Change is discrete succession, not identity transformation.","C) Electrons smoothly transform","D) Quantum jumps prove inherent identity"],"correct":"B","explanation":"Quantum jumps: state A ceases, state B begins — no smooth transformation of an enduring identity. Like the young man ceasing and the old man arising through dependent succession."},"advanced":{"question":"Why does the same identity/difference structure appear in Chapters 2, 10, 11, and 13?","options":["A) Nāgārjuna is repetitive","B) The logical structure is universal — it applies to any claim of inherent existence, whether the topic is motion, fire-fuel, time, or change. The universality proves the argument targets inherent existence itself, not specific topics.","C) Each chapter is unrelated","D) Only Ch.13 uses this structure"],"correct":"B","explanation":"The identity/difference analysis is Nāgārjuna's universal tool. Its repeated application across domains demonstrates that the problem is with inherent existence claims as such, not with specific topics."}},"verseText":"A thing itself does not change. Something different does not change. Because a young man doesn't grow old, And because and an old man doesn't grow old either.","madhyamakaConcept":"Identity horn: if the young man (as inherently young) becomes old, he retains his young-identity while being old — contradiction.
